question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $17,$ the additive inverse of $34$ modulo $17$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $34$ modulo $17$ is the integer $0\le x<17$ such that

$$
x+34≡0\,(\text{mod}\,17).
$$

First, note that $34≡2\cdot 17≡0\,(\text{mod}\,17),$ and $0+0≡0\,(\text{mod}\,17).$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $34$ modulo $17$ is $0.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
34+0≡2\cdot 17+0≡2\cdot 0+0≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,17)
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
